summary: Next to session 20 the island has come a long way: dense flora, a beach hut, a pond, generated creatures. Next to session 163 the overview is the same picture apart from the hour. The one new thing, a wooden land yacht at the top of the beach, is a solid obstacle: in Jump in, walking into it says 'Oof! Something's in the way', and E, F, Space, Q and pushing for 2 s don't move it a millimetre. All three mini games were won on the first try by a naive steering bot (fireflies 8/8 in 33 s, berries 12 to 1/0/1, hide and seek 4/4 in 21 s). The follow camera spent this review looking at pine needles, a swing post and the inside of the sail.

lighting.why: The raster at 13:00-13:24 is pleasant but flat: one sun, soft shadows, no light that is the subject. The traced live view (reviews/p166/traced.png) is still grainy, with navy-blue noisy cloud undersides and flat dark ellipses for cloud shadows on the sea. At noon the firefly catch has no visible fireflies at all (play/firefly-1.png). The session 163 progress shot at 04:00 showed lamp pools; nothing new was lit since.

materials.why: The canvas sail is a flat, evenly lit white panel in the raster (play/jump-yacht-2.png), in the post still, and as a white card on the horizon in the traced view. The wheels are solid brown discs and the deck is grey planks. The sea is still the only material that shows off the tracer. The waterfight and wire films are plastic on grey slabs.

world.why: From 163 to 166 the overview progress shot is unchanged apart from the time of day, and the yacht isn't even visible from it. Orbit and free views show a hard horizontal seam where the sea meets a flat pale band of sky (orbit-2.png, y≈118). Since session 20 the density has grown a lot, but the layout (cottage, pond, spiral path, pines) is the same island.

props.why: The generated assets (striped beach hut, cottage, pigs, driftwood, mushrooms) are fine, and the yacht uses generated planks and wheels. But the yacht stands with a cairn of stones in front of it, and Lumi's science builds in films are still primitives (white L-block boat, blue cans on a slab).

creatures.why: The cast is readable and charming up close: pig hats, the crab, the sheep, Lumi's spiky head and grumpy brows. The friends play tag, dance and swing on their own and cheer 'HIGHER!' (follow-2.png). But two of ten creature close-ups show only the inside of a tree crown (motion/p166live/creatures.png rows 3-4), and no creature goes near the new yacht.

animation.why: live_motion: 10/10 moving well. Lumi's idle strip has head turns and blinks without pops. The films show no snaps outside cuts. Nothing new was animated: there is no pose for Lumi touching, pushing or boarding the yacht, and walking into it just stops with an 'Oof' label.

fun.why: I played all four for a minute each with a naive bot that walks straight at the nearest target. Firefly catch: 8/8 in 33 s, 'A new best time!'. Berry race: 12 berries to the rivals' 1, 0 and 1 in 27 s. Hide and seek: 4/4 in 21 s. None of them is a contest. In Jump in, P paint showed nothing, hold-6 left Lumi standing inside a pine, and the yacht, the big new toy, can't be boarded, pushed or sailed. Down from 5: the newest thing on the island is the least playable.

wow.why: The last post is a still of a cart that 'doesn't sail yet', and the host judged it a repeat. Before it came six clay pots, a glowing wire and a motor that sticks: lab-bench recipes framed on slabs. A stranger would not share any of the last five.

camera.why: Follow mode over six shots: at 13:05 a pine trunk and crown, with 'Cumulus: That was fun!' printed on the needles (follow.png). At 13:23 the yacht's sail covers the left third of the frame while a swing post covers Lumi (follow-2.png). During firefly catch, the winning moment frames the hut roof with Lumi hidden behind it (play/firefly-over.png). Two creature close-ups are inside tree crowns.

ui.why: The panel is unchanged: long text, a 'Working towards ... 8 of 23 steps' plan read only by the author, and 'Things to try' that never mentions the yacht. The Jump in key strip lists 24 gags, several of which do nothing visible. Name labels draw over occluders. The mini game HUDs are clear (Fireflies 4/8, 46 s left, nearest 15 m ahead).

style.why: Glossy clay crowns and bubble bushes, generated realistic hut and driftwood, and flat-primitive science props still look like three different games. The yacht's grey planks match the hut, a small step toward one look.

performance.why: 30 fps held throughout four mini games. Frame median 4.2 ms, p95 9.2 ms, landyacht system 0.0 ms.

findings.title: The yacht on the beach is a wall: board it, push it, sail it, friends aboard
findings.what: In Jump in, Lumi walks up to the yacht and gets 'Oof! Something's in the way. Turn with A or D.' E, F, Space and Q do nothing, and holding W into it for 2 s leaves its position at (0.887, -18.104) unchanged. The sail force from the 3D box ran only in a separate test process. Five sessions of aerodynamics give a player nothing to do.
findings.evidence: reviews/p166/play/jump-yacht-0.png, jump-yacht-2.png, play/log.txt ('yacht after pushing into it: [0.887, -18.104, 0.835]')
findings.suggestion: Ship it imperfect: in Jump in, E boards, Q/E sheets in and out, A/D steers. The wheels turn by distance rolled, sand sprays off the tyres, and a friend leans out on the windward side and squeals when it heels. Pushing it rolls it by its mass. If the live GPU box can't keep up, use the solved CL/CD table from the 3D runs. Then film a 10 s chase along the beach.
findings.done_when: A play script presses E by the yacht, holds the sheet key for 10 s in an 8 m/s wind, and logs the yacht more than 15 m from where it started. A screenshot shows Lumi on the deck with the wheels turned, and 'Things to try' names the keys.

findings.title: Follow and close-up cameras sit inside trees, the sail and bodies
findings.what: In 3 of 6 follow shots, plus the firefly win screen, the subject is hidden: by a pine (13:05), by the yacht's sail filling a third of the frame and a swing post over Lumi (13:23), and by the hut roof at 'All caught!'. Two of ten creature close-ups are only the green inside of a tree crown.
findings.where: camera rig (follow), live_motion creature framing, mini game end shots
findings.suggestion: Cast a ray from target to camera against tree crown and trunk bounds, props and creature capsules each frame. Pull in or swing round with a smoothed spring, and fade the occluder if that fails. Frame the win moment on Lumi, not the map. Hide name labels whose owner is occluded.
findings.done_when: Ten follow screenshots 5 s apart and one per mini game win screen, with no frame where a prop, foliage or a body covers the subject or more than 25% of the view.

findings.title: The mini games are no contest: a naive bot wins all three on the first try
findings.what: A bot that walks straight at the nearest target wins every game in under 40 s: fireflies 8/8 in 33 s, berries 12 vs rivals 1/0/1, hide and seek 4/4 in 21 s. There is no skill, no risk and no reason to play twice. None of them uses the island's wind, sand, magnets or the yacht.
findings.suggestion: Replace one with a yacht race against a friend on a wind that turns: lose by over-sheeting, win by trimming. Make the berry rivals path-plan and steal from your bush, and have the hide and seek friends move when you look away.
findings.done_when: The same naive bot (reviews/p166/play.jl) loses at least one of three runs in at least two games, and one game uses the solved sail or the sand.

findings.title: The land yacht's sail is a white board: belly, light through canvas, spoked wheels
findings.what: Up close in the raster and in the post still, the sail is a flat, evenly lit white panel, and the wheels are solid brown discs. Nothing in it says canvas, rope or turned wood, and nothing shows what a path tracer can do with cloth backlit by the sun. In the traced overview it is a white card on the horizon.
findings.suggestion: Give the sail the camber the solver uses as real geometry. Use Hikari thin translucent diffuse transmission with a woven-normal texture and visible seams, so a low sun glows through it and the patch and tear show in silhouette. Add spoked wheels with iron tyres (real metal) and rope sheets. Take a traced still at 64+ spp against the evening sun.
findings.done_when: A traced still where the sail is visibly brighter on the shaded side from transmitted sun, has a curved belly in silhouette, and the wheels show spokes.

findings.title: Traced view: grainy, murky, fireflies are flat discs that light nothing
findings.what: Path tracing on in orbit at 13:08 after 25 s: visible grain everywhere, navy noisy cloud undersides, flat dark ellipses for cloud shadows on the sea, and grey-green crowns. It looks worse than the raster.
findings.suggestion: Denoise (OIDN) the accumulated frame. Make clouds a volume or a white two-sided diffuse with sky fill so their undersides aren't navy. Use a sky light from the same model as the raster.
findings.done_when: A traced screenshot of the orbit view after 25 s with no visible per-pixel grain at 100% and cloud undersides lighter than the sea.

findings.title: Jump in: most gag keys show nothing; the motor can't be found or flicked
findings.what: The key strip lists 24 gags. P paint showed nothing on screen. Hold-6 ('float a magnet top by the boards east of the kiln') ended with Lumi standing inside a pine with no top in sight.
findings.where: Jump in, plugins with gag keys
findings.suggestion: Cut the strip to the 6 gags that make something you see within 1 s. Make each leave a mark the world keeps (paint on what it hits, stomped sand), and walk Lumi to the station when its key is held.
findings.done_when: A screenshot after each listed key shows its effect within 1 s, and hold-6 shows the top floating in frame.

findings.title: Posts are bench experiments on slabs: make one a player would share
findings.what: The last eight posts are copper, iron, wire, a coil and pots, mostly stills or films of small objects on grey or green slabs. The newest was judged a repeat. Films still show a white L-block boat and blue cylinders on a slate slab that starts on a black frame.
findings.evidence: reviews/motion/perfectionist-0166/wire-spins-itself-steps.jpg, workshop-boat-overview.jpg; host judge ×0.22 on 'My land yacht'
findings.suggestion: Leave the bench once. Film a moment with creatures, consequence and a joke: the yacht dragging a squealing pig across the sand, sail backlit at sunset, a crash into the cairns. Cut it like a short, not a lab record. Re-shoot or retire the primitive films.
findings.done_when: A post whose film has at least two creatures reacting on screen, no black or bare-slab frame, and a traced sunset or lamp-lit shot. The white L-block and slab films are replaced.

findings.title: A hard seam where the sea meets the sky in orbit and free views
findings.what: In orbit and free views the sea ends in a ruler-straight edge against a flat pale band, with no haze blend. It reads like a backdrop card behind the island.
findings.suggestion: Blend the far sea into the sky with distance fog in the sea's colour and a brighter horizon band. Add a distant island or sail on the horizon for depth.
findings.done_when: An orbit screenshot where a column of pixels through the horizon changes brightness smoothly over ≥10 px, with no step larger than 15/255.

engine.what: Live path tracing gives a grainy, navy-shadowed image after 25 s, with no denoiser in the live view

process: The author works seriously and honestly: the journal admits the 2D slices stalled backwards and checks 3D against CPU to three digits. But five sessions (162-166) went into sail aerodynamics a player never sees. The progress shots from 163 to 166 are the same picture, and the one new object is an obstacle you bump into. Goal 3 (physics to play with) moved in the lab only. Goals 1 (interactions) and 2 (a proud traced film) have not moved: the mini games are still trivially won and nothing new reacts to the player. Goals 4/6/7 (rendering, light, materials) got only a sewn patch. Goal 5 (Lumi's garden) got the yacht as a wish come true. Goal 8 (radical ideas) lost ground: the host judged the post a repeat, and Lumi is bored and annoyed at 1.0. Next session, stop refining the solver and put the yacht into play with whatever forces it has. Let the player board it and a friend ride along, and film the result in light that shows the canvas. A sailing toy that is 30% wrong and fun beats a correct number in a log.
